build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player interacts with cooking stations by clicking to place ingredients and initiate cooking processes with visible timers or progress indicators. Score 0 if there are no interactive stations.
Orders arrive with recipe requirements and countdown timers; failing to complete an order before timeout loses it with visible negative feedback. Score 0 if no order system exists.
Recipes require multiple steps at different stations in a specific order (chop, cook, assemble, plate), and the player must manage the sequence. Score 0 if recipes are single-step.
Overcooking or burning food wastes ingredients with visible smoke/fire feedback, requiring the player to monitor multiple timers simultaneously. Score 0 if food cannot be overcooked.
Completing orders earns coins and tips based on speed, which fund upgrades between shifts. Score 0 if no economy exists.
At least 5 distinct cooking stations (chopping board, stove, fryer, oven, plating area) with different interaction mechanics. Score 0 if only one station exists.
At least 8 distinct recipes with different ingredient combinations and station sequences, unlocked progressively. Score 0 if only one recipe exists.
Between-shift upgrades offer station improvements (faster stove, larger fryer), new recipe unlocks, and kitchen expansions with at least 5 options. Score 0 if no upgrade system exists.
At least 10 shifts with escalating difficulty: more simultaneous orders, complex recipes, shorter timers, and higher customer expectations. Score 0 if difficulty never increases.
A shift summary shows orders completed, orders failed, tips earned, star rating, and total coins with retry or continue options. Score 0 if shifts end abruptly with no summary.
Normal startup shows a styled title screen with the game name, restaurant storefront imagery, and a Start control. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The flow connects title to shift start to kitchen gameplay to shift summary to upgrade shop without restarting the executable. Score 0 if major transitions are missing.

The HUD clearly shows active orders with recipes and timers, current station states, and coins earned in readable non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the player cannot determine what to cook or order status.

Player actions produce visible feedback: placing ingredients shows them on stations, cooking shows progress, burning shows smoke, completing orders shows success animation, and tips flash. Score 0 if actions happen silently.

Art direction is coherent across title, kitchen, stations, food items, orders, HUD, and menus with a consistent restaurant palette and style. Score 0 if mostly default controls or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
Cooking stations, ingredients, prepared dishes, kitchen equipment, and order tickets use real sprite art with appetizing distinct designs. Score 0 if primary elements are unstyled rectangles.
Animation brings the kitchen to life: cooking bubbles, chopping motion, fire flickering, steam rising, plating assembly, and order-complete celebrations. Score 0 if all elements are static.
HUD and UI panels use styled themed widgets with chalkboard menus, recipe cards, or restaurant-styled elements rather than raw HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if all UI is default Label/Button.
